K1.stone_why: Moderate faceting on bowls (B, e, 6, O) gives a hewn, inscriptional feel over a classical serif skeleton.
K1.carving_why: Facets are applied evenly across letters and digits and stay crisp, with 1/7, 3/8 and 0/O clearly distinct, though some curves read slightly polygonal.
K1.calm_why: Steady and grounded with good presence; the facets add a little edge but nothing shouts.

K2.stone_why: Strong, visible facets on every bowl make the display text read clearly as cut stone.
K2.carving_why: Facets are coarse and large enough that curves (e, s, 6, 5) start to look low-poly rather than chiselled, though digits remain distinguishable.
K2.calm_why: Calm overall, but the heavier angularity adds some visual noise at large sizes.

K3.stone_why: Faceting is subtle and mostly reads as a classical serif with only a hint of cut stone.
K3.carving_why: What carving there is is clean and consistent, but it is barely visible at display size so it contributes little.
K3.calm_why: Very calm and composed with full presence, close to a refined book serif.

K4.stone_why: The most convincingly hewn: angular bowls, faceted counters and diamond-like dots read as an inscription cut into stone.
K4.carving_why: The faceting is one coherent system carried through letters, digits and punctuation, with digits easy to tell apart, though the largest bowls get somewhat coarse.
K4.calm_why: Grounded with strong presence; the angularity is firm but not aggressive.

K5.stone_why: Clear, medium-strength facets give a carved feel similar to K1.
K5.carving_why: Facets are consistent and crisp across letters and figures with no broken shapes, and the digit pairs stay distinct.
K5.calm_why: Balanced and steady, with presence and only mild angular tension.

K6.stone_why: Smooth, uncarved classical serif; grounded through its serifs and weight but not stone-like.
K6.calm_why: Fully calm and composed with good presence from the bold weights.
